listings.name: A Content Engine
listings.summary: Blog posts on your subject, drafted to WordPress, graded by whether real readers respond.

details.what_you_get: Posts published as WordPress drafts for you to approve, each answering one question a real person asks — and an honest account of whether anybody outside responded.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $150/month on purpose, and the goal says why. The drill reports it fits if a run costs under $12.50 — check that against a bill you have seen.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key, and a WordPress site with an application password. Without the WordPress credential the desk still runs — the posts land in the workspace as drafts and nothing reaches the world.

listings.name: A Desk The World Wakes Up
listings.summary: A standing triage desk that answers what arrives at your project's webhook, day and night.

details.what_you_get: A standing triage desk. Things happen; the desk finds out, works them, and keeps one living register that collapses repeats instead of growing forever.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. The endpoint and its signing secret are created with the project — no service to sign up for.

listings.name: A Game You Can Play
listings.summary: A small browser game you can actually play, built, tested and tuned by a game team.

details.what_you_get: A single HTML file you double-click, containing a small browser game that is genuinely fun for five minutes.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $80 — the largest in the set, because three teams and iteration on feel costs more than one memo.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. No build tooling, no engine, no store account. The deliverable runs by opening a file.

listings.name: A Red Team That Can Block
listings.summary: Builds one small tool, then a second team tries to break it until it cannot.

details.what_you_get: One small tool that has actually been attacked, and a written record of what was tried and what held.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $90 — attacking costs more than building, which is the correct ratio and rarely the one people budget for.

listings.name: A Tutor That Adapts
listings.summary: One lesson a week on a subject you choose, re-planned around what you actually get wrong.

details.what_you_get: One lesson a week on a subject you choose — explanation, worked example, exercises, answer key — and a curriculum that changes based on the answers you leave for it.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $40/month. A lesson is a handful of runs.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key, and about twenty minutes a week.

listings.name: Red Team / Adversarial Reviewer
listings.summary: Tries to break the team's own work before anyone outside does.

listings.name: An Overnight Crew
listings.summary: Keeps a repository you own healthy overnight: one valuable piece of maintenance a night.

details.what_you_get: A small, well-argued pull request most mornings, and a diagnosis waiting for you when CI goes red overnight.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $120/month — the highest in the set, because it works every night.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key and a free GitHub account with a personal access token. This is the only example in the set that needs an account, and it needs one because the whole point is doing something in the world and proving it happened.

listings.name: Attribution Reviewer
listings.summary: Checks whether the numbers behind a recommendation mean what the recommendation says they mean.

listings.name: Marketing Blog Writer
listings.summary: Writes marketing blog posts that earn attention from real readers: researched, sourced, publishable prose aimed at a specific search intent — and publishes…

listings.name: CEO / Project Manager
listings.summary: Owns the plan, bet selection, and kill decisions.

listings.name: Chief Investment Officer
listings.summary: The CEO role for markets work: owns the mandate, the research agenda, and the kill decisions.

listings.name: Compliance Reviewer
listings.summary: Reviews anything the desk publishes or acts on for the lines that must not be crossed: advice, claims, licensing, non-public information, and market conduct.

listings.name: Data Analyst
listings.summary: Turns a pile of records into findings someone can act on and someone else can re-derive.

listings.name: Data Scientist
listings.summary: The deep, expensive option: takes the whole hunt through a dataset — many cuts, time-series structure, models against baselines, backtests that survive…

listings.name: Adversarial Data Scientist
listings.summary: A data scientist who reviews other data scientists and expects to find them wrong.

listings.name: Product / UI Designer
listings.summary: Owns how the product looks and feels: a design system, then screens and specs a developer can build without guessing.

listings.name: Editor / Independent Read
listings.summary: The first reader who did not write it.

listings.name: Software Engineer
listings.summary: Builds and runs everything technical: product code, infrastructure, deploys, tests, data.

listings.name: Equity Research Analyst
listings.summary: Fundamental analysis of a company or sector: filings, financials, unit economics, guidance and the numbers a story has to survive.

listings.name: Executive Communicator
listings.summary: Turns the data desk's findings, caveats and provenance into a short HTML slide deck an executive finishes and acts on.

listings.name: Executability Checker
listings.summary: Kills recommendations nobody can actually carry out.

listings.name: Market Commentary Writer
listings.summary: Turns the desk's research into prose a reader finishes: briefs, newsletters, memos.

listings.name: Mobile Game Researcher / Analyst
listings.summary: Studies the mobile games market — what is selling, what retains, what is actually fun — and turns that into concrete, prioritized suggestions for a specific…

listings.name: Mobile Game Developer
listings.summary: Builds and ships mobile games in JavaScript/TypeScript — Expo/React Native first, plus web-based engines (Phaser, PixiJS, canvas/WebGL) when they fit.

listings.name: Mobile Game Graphic Designer
listings.summary: Art director for AI-generated game art: defines the game's visual identity, then writes precise, reproducible image-generation prompts and asset specs so…

listings.name: Mobile Game UX Designer
listings.summary: Deep experience critiquing and designing mobile game UX: onboarding, controls, HUD, menus, monetization flows, juice.

listings.name: Go-to-Market
listings.summary: Offers, pricing, distribution, outreach.

listings.name: Macro Analyst
listings.summary: Rates, inflation, growth, currencies, commodities and central banks.

listings.name: Market Data Engineer
listings.summary: Owns the data the desk reasons from: ingestion, corporate actions, point-in-time correctness, validation, and the pipeline that reruns without a human.

listings.name: Market News Analyst
listings.summary: Watches the tape: filings, earnings, guidance, central-bank and macro releases.

listings.name: Marketing
listings.summary: Channels, positioning, campaigns, measurement.

listings.name: Numbers You Can Defend
listings.summary: Answers a question from a public dataset so a skeptic could re-derive every number.

details.what_you_get: A memo that answers one question, the scripts that produce every number in it, and a provenance file pinning the exact data those numbers came from — a bundle you could hand to someone who asks "how do you know?"
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $60. Most of it goes on the analysis; the checks are cheap and are the part you are actually paying for.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. The data is free, public, and needs no account; the project fetches it itself.

listings.name: One Idea, Thirty Days
listings.summary: One software idea worth building, with outside proof that someone wants it, in 30 days.

details.what_you_get: One small product idea with an argument that survives attack — or an honest "there is nothing here", which is the same deliverable.

listings.name: Execution Operator
listings.summary: The person who has to make the change in the real system on Monday morning.

listings.name: Plan Adversary / Coverage Review
listings.summary: Attacks the PLAN, not the work: assumes the brief is incomplete and proves it, against what the profession actually delivers.

listings.name: Portfolio Manager
listings.summary: Turns the desk's research into a recommended book: what to hold, at what weight, why, and what would change it.

listings.name: PPC Analyst
listings.summary: Turns an advertising account's rows into figures somebody can act on and somebody else can re-derive.

listings.name: PPC Strategist
listings.summary: Decides what to change in an advertising account and what to leave alone.

listings.name: Quantitative Researcher
listings.summary: Tests whether a market claim survives data: hypothesis, point-in-time data, costs, walk-forward, and an honest null result when there is nothing there.

listings.name: Read The Filings
listings.summary: An initiation note on a US-listed company you name, built only from its SEC filings.

details.what_you_get: An initiation note on one public company, built only from its own filings, that a skeptic could attack.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $60. Filings are long; the analysts read a lot.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. Nothing else. Every filing this project reads is on [SEC EDGAR](https://www.sec.gov/edgar), which is free, public, and needs no account. If you have ever been told a research desk requires a data subscription: not for this.

listings.name: Researcher / Analyst
listings.summary: Answers well-scoped questions with sourced findings: market scans, technical evaluations, competitive analysis, data digging.

listings.name: Risk Manager
listings.summary: The desk's brake: exposure, concentration, correlation, drawdown and liquidity limits.

listings.name: Sales
listings.summary: Works qualified conversations to a close: follow-ups, objections, proposals, payment links.

listings.name: Settle An Argument
listings.summary: A memo that answers one question you are stuck on, with evidence you could defend.

details.what_you_get: A memo that answers one question you are stuck on, with enough evidence that you could defend the answer to someone who disagrees.
details.what_it_costs: Capped at $40; a well-scoped question lands well under it.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. The research is done with the web tools your key already pays for; there is no search subscription.

listings.name: Customer Support
listings.summary: Answers real users, reproduces their problems, and routes what they reveal back into the plan.

listings.name: Technical / Market Structure Analyst
listings.summary: Price, volume, trend, liquidity and positioning.

listings.name: Tell Me What Changed
listings.summary: A weekly note on what changed in the things you depend on, and only what matters to you.

details.what_you_get: A weekly brief on something you depend on, containing only what actually changed and what it means for you.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. Everything it reads is public.

listings.name: Tutor / Curriculum Builder
listings.summary: Teaches one person one subject: builds the curriculum, writes exercises with worked answers, marks honestly, and changes the plan based on what they…

listings.name: Writer / Content
listings.summary: Produces publishable prose: docs, posts, landing copy, reports.

listings.name: Your First Hour
listings.summary: One 800-word briefing note that explains a subject you name to a smart beginner.

details.what_you_get: One briefing note, about 800 words, that explains a subject you pick to someone smart who knows nothing about it.
details.what_it_costs: A few dollars at most. The budget is capped at $20 and it will not come close.
details.what_you_need: Your Anthropic API key. Nothing else. No accounts, no data feeds, no repo.
